Hi Naomi / Kimberly,

- DPF alignment (cross-border transfer assurances to EU controllers)

Hi Lina,

Thanks — attaching what you requested. Quick summary up front:

- Attached: redwood_dpa_annex_v1.pdf (draft DPA annex), control-matrix-medalign.xlsx (controls mapped to DPF/Schrems II considerations), subprocessor-list-20280718.csv
- KMS: keys for customer data at rest are by default managed in our cloud KMS (AWS KMS in eu-west-1 for EU customers). We offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via customer-managed CMKs for Private deployments and Dedicated customers; we support HSM-backed keys through partner integrations for enterprise private deployments.
- Cross-border routing: for EU controller data we pin inference and logs to eu regions; fallbacks are documented and require explicit agreement in the annex.
- Subprocessor notifications: quarterly bulletin + ad-hoc notifications for material changes; we provide a signed subprocessor addendum on request.
- Retention: configurable retention window; default logs retained 90 days, KV/prefix cache ephemeral (max 30 days) unless customer configures a longer persistence in Dedicated/Private. For your 36-month requirement we can accommodate via Private or Dedicated with contractual addendum — see page 3 of the DPA annex.

I’ve called out the two likely policy gaps for an EU controller with a 36-month retention demand: (1) BYOK/HSM is available but requires Private/Dedicated, (2) KV cache persistence beyond 90 days is non-standard and needs ops changes and SLA addendum.

Please see the attached bundle. Happy to hop on a short call to run through the KMS flow and what a BYOK onboarding timeline looks like.

Best,

Naomi Feldman
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Hi Lina — quick follow-ups after Naomi’s bundle:

> On 2028-07-18 Naomi Feldman wrote:
> > KMS: keys for customer data at rest are by default managed in our cloud KMS (AWS KMS in eu-west-1 for EU customers). We offer BYOK...

Two practical clarifications you asked about:

1) BYOK timeline: for Dedicated we can enable BYOK in ~4 weeks after SOW and exchange of key material instructions; for Private (customer-managed infra) timeline depends on your infra team and audit schedule — typically 6–10 weeks including validation.
2) Key custody model: for BYOK on Dedicated we hold only wrapped keys; customer retains key policy and can request rotation. We can provide HSM-backed key proofs during onboarding (attestation of HSM vendor, FIPS level, and key lifecycle docs).
3) Subprocessor CSV: the attached list includes planned subprocessor classification and hosting regions. If you need contractual guarantees for specific subprocessors we can convert those to explicit addenda.

I’ve included a short attachments summary in the control matrix (column H) that maps each control to evidence artifacts and the expected lead for follow-up (Security, Product, or Ops).

If helpful, Ben (cc’d) can loop in product engineering to demo the BYOK flow and a short retention config walkthrough.

—Kimberly

Kimberly Park
Sr. PM, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi / Kimberly — that is very helpful. A couple quick asks so our legal and security teams can proceed: 

- Can you produce a one-page diagram of key flow for BYOK (wrap/unwarp + who rotates)?
- Can you confirm the SLA commitment for data residency (i.e., written confirmation that EU controller data will not be processed outside eu regions without prior consent)?
- Please confirm any additional cost items for BYOK/HSM and extended retention (rough order of magnitude).

If you can send the one-pager and the cost ROIs by EOD 2028-07-21 we’ll include them in our RFP packet. After that we’ll book a short 30-min call to resolve any final legal redlines.

Best —
Lina
